summary: Frank E. Reynolds (1930–2019) worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He served as a professor at the University of Chicago from circa 1967 until 2019.

Frank F. Conlon (1938–2021) was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Minnesota (1969) and was Professor Emeritus at the University of Washington from circa 2002 to 2021.

Frank J. Hoffman works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa under Stewart R. Sutherland, Eliot Deutsch, David J. Kalupahana, Prithwish Neogy, Rama Nath Sharma, and K. N. Upadhyaya.

Frank Lee Woodward (1871–1952) worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Christ's Hospital and Sidney Sussex College under Caroline Rhys Davids, and later served as Dekan at Mahinda College (1903–1919) and translator for the Pali Text Society (circa 1919).

Frank Raymond Allchin (1923–2010) was an Indology and archaeology scholar. He earned his BA at SOAS under Kenneth de Burgh Codrington, taught at SOAS (1954–1959) and the University of Cambridge (1959–1989), and was affiliated with the Ancient India and Iran Trust.

Frank-Richard Hamm (1920–1973) specialized in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his doctorate at the University of Hamburg under Walther Schubring, later lecturing there (1948–1952, 1957–1964) before becoming a professor at the University of Bonn in 1965.

Franklin Edgerton (1885–1963) was an Indologist and linguist who earned his PhD at Johns Hopkins under Maurice Bloomfield. He held professorships at the University of Pennsylvania (1913–1926) and Yale University (1926–1953), also visiting Harvard and Banaras Hindu University.

Franz Altheim (1898–1976) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Goethe University Frankfurt, later holding posts there (circa 1928–1943), at Halle-Wittenberg (circa 1943–1950), and at the Free University of Berlin (circa 1950–1964).

Franz Aubrey Metcalf specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Chicago and served as an instructor at California State University, Los Angeles (attested 2002–2006).

Franz Bernhard (1931–1971) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied under Ernst Waldschmidt at the University of Göttingen, habilitated at Goethe University Frankfurt, and served as a professor at the University of Hamburg from 1966 to 1971.

Franz Boas (1858–1942) was a linguist and anthropologist who studied at Heidelberg, Bonn, and Kiel, and under Wilhelm Wundt. He held posts at Clark University, the American Museum of Natural History, and Columbia University (circa 1896–1942).

Franz Bopp (1791–1867) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Karl Windischmann, Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy, and Antoine-Léonard de Chézy. He held the Chair of Sanskrit at Humboldt University of Berlin from 1821 to 1867.

Franz Ferdinand Benary (1805–1880) studied Indology at Bonn, Halle-Wittenberg, and Humboldt University of Berlin under Franz Bopp. He served at Humboldt University of Berlin as a lecturer from 1829 and as an associate professor in theology from 1831.

Franz Ferdinand Schwarz (1934–2001) was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Graz from circa 1953 to 1958 and later served there as a professor from circa 1976 to 1999.

Franz Heinrich Trithen (1820–1854) was a linguist and Indologist who studied under Franz Bopp at Humboldt University of Berlin. He worked at the British Museum (circa 1844–1848) and was a professor of modern languages at Oxford (circa 1848–1854).

Franz Kielhorn (1840–1908) was an Indologist who studied under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler, Albrecht Weber, and Theodor Benfey. He served as Professor of Oriental Languages at Deccan College (1866–1881) before holding the Indology chair at the University of Göttingen from 1881.
Franz Xaver Erhard is a Tibetologist. He completed his MA studies at the Free University of Berlin and Humboldt University of Berlin, and earned his PhD from the University of Bonn (attested 2003).

Franz von Erdmann (1793–1862) was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He studied at the University of Rostock (circa 1812–1817) and held a post at Kazan Imperial University from circa 1818 to 1845.

Franz-Karl Ehrhard is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his degrees at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen. He served as Resident Representative for the Nepal Research Centre (1988–1993) and Professor at the University of Munich (2001–2019).

François Gros (1933–2021) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at the University of Lyon from circa 1950 to 1955 and later held a post at the École Pratique des Hautes Études from circa 1977 to 2002.
